Social, Moral, Spiritual & Cultural - Personal Development
At All Saints Church School we recognise that the personal development of pupils, spiritually, morally, socially and culturally plays a significant part in their ability to learn and achieve.
Provide a balanced, engaging and broad education that gives our children opportunities to explore and develop their own, values and beliefs, spiritual awareness.
Encourage a positive and caring attitude towards other people; an understanding of British Values and its social and cultural traditions as well as an appreciation of the diversity and richness of other cultures.
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development is promoted, not only through all the subjects of the curriculum, but also through the ethos of the school and our shared values.
Please click on the Link Here for SMSC Policy
As a school, we use a scheme called Scarf to support us in our teaching.
Scarf is more than a PSHE Scheme of Work. It provides a structured programme of personal development to nurture the ‘whole child’ and increase learning capacity, underpinned by mindfulness philosophy and practice.
SCARF's whole-school approach supports us by giving us everything we need to meet the new Relationships Education and Health Education statutory requirements. More than just a PSHE scheme of work, SCARF supports great learning every day. SCARF represents our values for children of Safety, Caring, Achievement, Resilience and Friendship.
Meeting all DfE requirements for statutory Relationships and Health Education, and mapped to the PSHE Association's Programme of Study, SCARF is a framework consisting of lesson plans, online planning, assessment and Ofsted tools to give busy teachers skills and confidence to embed a comprehensive Relationships and Health Education, PSHE Education and Wellbeing programme throughout the primary years. SCARF is a whole-school approach to promoting behaviour, safety, achievement and well-being.
At All Saints Church School, we believe that the wellbeing of our pupils is the foundation for successful learning and personal growth. We are committed to creating a nurturing environment where every child feels safe, valued, and supported to thrive both academically and emotionally, becoming the best version of themselves.
Our approach to wellbeing is woven into every aspect of school life—from our curriculum and pastoral care to our daily routines and relationships. We encourage our children to develop through our values of wisdom, love, friendship, perseverance, respect and community, helping them to become confident and caring individuals.
As part of our commitment to preparing pupils for life in modern Britain, we actively promote the fundamental British values of:
Democracy – encouraging pupil voice and participation in decision-making.
The Rule of Law – helping children understand the importance of rules and laws in keeping everyone safe and fair.
Individual Liberty – supporting children to make informed choices and express themselves freely and responsibly.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance – fostering respect for others, celebrating diversity, and promoting understanding of different cultures and beliefs.
Together, our focus on wellbeing and British values helps children to grow into respectful, responsible citizens who are ready to contribute positively to their communities and the wider world.
At All Saints some of the ways we promote British values are:
Voting for our school council -this teaches our children about fair voting, campaigning, and the importance of having a voice.
Voting for house captains – Year 6 write their presentations to their colour houses
Music and art ambassadors
Our youngest children vote for which story book they would like to hear
Children vote and make collaborative decisions about choosing the class reward when they have achieved the correct number of merits
Pupil voice : our children give feedback on the school environment – e.g. the playground reset- this shows that their opinions matter and can influence change.
The school council vote on which charity to support or how to contribute to local causes.
Our Year 2 and Year 5 children take part in the Archbishop Young Leaders award where they decide who to support and how
We believe in our school value of respect
We use SLANT across the school to promote active listening, engagement, and positive behaviour.
S – Sit up: Encourages good posture to show readiness to learn.
L – Listen: Focus on the speaker and pay attention.
A – Ask and answer questions: Be involved in the lesson by participating.
N – Nod your head: Show understanding and engagement.
T – Track the speaker: Follow the speaker with your eyes to stay focused
We respect our play leaders
We share and take turns
We wear a neat school uniform
We know to be ready, respectful and safe
We look after equipment
We respect the environment and want to make a positive impact (e.g. Through our pollinator project)
We respect others’ beliefs
We learn about different faiths
We know that our school is a safe place to make mistakes
We do not judge others
We have buddies (Year 6 and Acorn children)
We are inclusive in our play – we are encouraged to play with everyone
We celebrate diversity through displays, multicultural events such as World Cultures Day and we have inclusive reading books
We learn that unkind behaviour and bullying is wrong through our SCARF sessions and anti-bullying week.
We have a Chinese extra-curricular club
Collective worship helps our understanding of global issues and differences
Our staff model and encourage respectful language when talking about others, helping children understand how to speak kindly and thoughtfully.
We have the freedom in our school to be true to ourselves
We use our values to make good choices
We try to never leave anyone out
We are given opportunities to choose tasks, reading books, or topics for projects, helping us to develop independence
Our children are encouraged to share their thoughts in class discussions, debates, and circle time, learning that their voice matters
We celebrate individuality and individual talents through events such as All Saints Got Talent
We have clear rules within our school, where we have consistent approaches and consequences
We respect our school values
Our rules are set to keep us safe
We have a clear behaviour matrix
Our play leaders help to keep us safe
We are ready, respectful and safe in school
Our Year 6 take part in a mock trial at the Yeovil Magistrate’s Court Mock Trial Competition. This involves a group of children representing All Saints Church school in different roles, such as: usher, magistrate, defence solicitor, defendant, defence witness, witness care, press reporter and court artist. It is an exciting venture that inspires children to witness different jobs and experience a real life trial scenario
When conflicts arise, we use restorative practices to help our children reflect on their actions, understand the impact, and make amends

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints Church School  - Our Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
Jesus says, “All things are possible if you believe.”
At All Saints Church School, our goal is to love and follow Jesus as our “Good Shepherd” (John 10: 14-16). We are guided by his teaching to “Love God and love others” (Mark 12: 30-31) and the Bible tells us that Jesus said, “All things are possible if you believe.” (Mark 9:23) This is the foundation of our ethos and values we live by as a school community.
Through lived experiences, we challenged the chosen theology, with a particular focus on the word “possible.” Together, we now understand that each person’s unique God given gifts, enable each individual and our community to flourish in accordance with God’s will, in keeping with the Trust vision “That they may have life, life in all its fullness.” John 10:10.
We aim to be the best version of ourselves in our daily lives through: worship, prayer, spirituality, work and play, following the teaching of the Good Shepherd, embodying his values.
The philosophy for learning at our school is summarised in our school vision statement and links to the Church of England's vision for education; educating for hope, community, wisdom and dignity.
All Saints Church School Vision
Jesus says, “All things are possible if you believe.”
And we believe that by working together, we can grow the very best, bespoke version of All Saints Church School.
If we can ignite, inspire and nurture curiosity and creativity, self-motivation and self-confidence, then
All things will be possible if we believe…
If we value and nurture the sparkle of all individuals, in a safe learning environment, with equality underpinning all efforts, children will be able to be the best version of themselves, valuing their own self-worth, knowing that
All things will be possible if we believe…
If we create a culture of compassion, trust and shared values, ensuring we all work together – both within the school and as part of the wider community - then
All things will be possible if we believe…
If, by utilising an extraordinarily talented team of adults, we can encourage trial and error to help develop resilience and perseverance, our children will become lifelong learners and
All things will be possible if we believe…
If by peeling back the layers of understanding we have a greater wisdom of life; little by little, deeper and deeper and day by day,
“All things will be possible if we believe,”
And we believe it is!
On a recent Vision and Values day, our children created a 100 word vision
We believe by helping each other, we can grow to be the very best. Our community cares and nurtures all children in a safe learning environment by being open-minded to curiosity and creativity. We always show respect, love and perseverance to everyone within our school. ​
LIKE THE GOOD SHEPHERD, if we remember all our school values and our individual gifts from God, we can build upon our wisdom for the greater community. Within a culture of compassion and friendship, we can become the best versions of ourselves! When we work together, we can make everything possible. All things will be possible if we believe.
We are part of the Bath and Wells Multi Academy Trust.
The Trust has the vision of providing an excellent education for every child, enhanced by a distinctive Christian ethos within the Trust family.
It holds values which we also believe to be fundamental to the growth of our children:
Educational and Aspirational Values
Moral and Christian Values
Collaborative Values.
"That they may have life, life in all its fullness." John 10:10
Our Christian Values
During the year 2022 All Saints Church School reviewed their Christian vision and values. This was an in-depth process that unified the opinions and thoughts from all members of the school community.
An Ethos committee, led by school leaders, helps to focus and embed our core values.
In June 2022, governors were invited to join classes across the school, gaining a deeper understanding of how the provision for children supported the understanding and embedding of each of our six Christian values;
Friendship, Love, Respect, Community, Perseverance and Wisdom.
Classes were each given a value to explore, and each class created an artistic representation in poster form.
Each governor now has a value assigned to them and they advocate for their value to ensure it is well embedded in school practice.
Our values form a focus during collective worship, in personal and social education, our wider curriculum, within our school rules and in the way we treat each other. Each half-term we focus on one of our values, reflecting on how we can improve life for all and how the Bible is a resource when learning about these values.

Christian Distinctiveness
Jesus says, “All things are possible, if you believe.” Mark 9:23
By working together, we can grow to be the very best version of ourselves here at All Saints Church School. By nurturing confidence, curiosity and a joy of learning, we believe that every child and adult can flourish.
When we work together in faith and purpose, all things will be possible if we believe.
Church and Clergy Involvement
At All Saints Church School, our relationships with the church and clergy play a vital role in living out our Christian Vision that “All things are possible if you believe.” Rooted in the example of the Good Shepherd, these partnerships strengthen our shared commitment to nurturing every child’s potential through worship, community and spiritual growth. The involvement of our church family helps us create worship that reflects our core values, deepens pupils’ understanding of faith in action and supports the flourishing of the whole school community.
Collective Worship
Collective Worship at All Saints Church School is an important part of our day. As a Church school, our time together as a school community is invaluable when sharing and understanding the views and traditions of the Church. Our Christian Vision and Values are embedded throughout all worship. Each half-term we focus on a value, giving time for thoughtful reflection.
Each act of worship is slightly different, and children can expect to sing, listen to stories, act out stories, listen to musicians and enjoy an interactive period of learning and reflection. Collective Worship is led by a variety of people here at All Saints Church School.
Visiting Worship Leaders
Reverend Nick, from St Catherine’s Church, regularly leads whole school worship, as do all of our teachers. Pupils are offered the opportunity to plan and lead class worship using our half‑termly Christian value as their guide. On a Friday we hold a ‘Praise and Share’ Collective Worship, where we invite parents to join us.
We are also extremely fortunate to have Daniel England visit our school monthly. He is a visiting Pastor from Vine Youth Ministry. Daniel’s ‘Mini Mix’ Collective Worships are lively and enjoyable; his guitar playing inspires us all to join in. Daniel’s inspirational storytelling helps our children to gain an even greater understanding of fundamental Christian values.
Open the Book
Open the Book also visit our school each week to lead collective worship. They provide children with a visual opportunity to hear key Bible stories, told by a team of Christians from our local Churches. Each drama presentation connects with the imagination of our children and takes around 10–15 minutes. It is a three-year rolling programme with an additional, along with the option of an additional year of materials based on Christian values for schools.
Community Links
All Saints Church School enjoys strong and longstanding links with the four churches in our Benefice, helping to deepen our Christian Vision and strengthen our sense of community. These partnerships support our worship life, our shared values and our connection to the local church family.

LOVE, WISDOM, PERSEVERANCE, FRIENDSHIP, COMMUNITY, RESPECT
How Our Christian Vision Shapes School Life
At All Saints Church School, our Christian Vision sits at the heart of everything we do and shapes the way we live, learn and grow as a community. Rooted in Jesus’ teaching and guided by the promise that “All things are possible if you believe,” our Vision inspires us to nurture the unique, gift of every child and adult. It influences our relationships, our choices and the way we care for one another, ensuring that kindness, respect, compassion and responsibility form the foundations of daily school life. In following the example of the Good Shepherd, we seek to create an environment in which everyone feels known, valued and supported to flourish morally, socially, spiritually and academically.
Our curriculum, worship and pastoral care are all shaped by this Vision and by the values that flow from it. Learning is designed to encourage curiosity, creativity, resilience and wisdom, helping pupils to understand their place in the wider world and how their actions can make a positive difference. Daily Collective Worship deepens pupils’ understanding of faith in action, connecting biblical teaching with real life experiences and strengthening our shared sense of hope, purpose and community. Through these lived experiences, our Christian Vision continues to guide us as we work together to become the very best version of All Saints Church School, believing that, through God’s love, “all things are possible.”
For more information about how our Christian Vision and Values please follow the link Our Vision and Values page.
Religious Education - All Saints Church School
At All Saints Church School, Religious Education (RE) is taught as a carefully planned and progressive subject that reflects our Christian Vision and supports pupils in developing a deep understanding of Christianity, alongside a respectful awareness of other faiths and world views. Our long and medium term plans ensure that learning builds securely over time, allowing pupils to revisit, embed and extend key theological concepts, biblical knowledge and spiritual reflection as they move through the school. Each unit is chosen and structured to support pupils in exploring big questions, developing curiosity, and making meaningful connections between faith, life and the wider world.
Through this structured approach, RE remains fully integrated into the broader ethos of the school, supporting pupils’ moral, social and spiritual development. Our curriculum draws on high quality resources and follows a clear sequence that encourages pupils to think deeply, reflect personally and engage with the Christian narrative that underpins our school community. This ensures that RE at All Saints Church School is both academically well structured and spiritually enriching, helping every child to grow in wisdom, understanding and appreciation of diverse beliefs. In addition, pupils experience further spiritual development through Godly Play sessions and floor books, which both offer reflective opportunities to explore faith, wonder and biblical stories in a thoughtful and child centred way.

Pupils contribute meaningfully to school life and support the values that underpin our Christian Vision. These responsibilities promote service, responsibility and active participation within our school community. They also demonstrate the structured opportunities pupils have to develop leadership, confidence and a strong sense of responsibility within the wider school community.

Shared Language of Spirituality
At All Saints Church School, the whole school community shares a clear and consistent understanding of spirituality, rooted in our Christian Vision. Pupils are encouraged to notice, reflect and respond to the world around them through experiences that inspire a sense of wonder, curiosity and personal thought. This includes quiet reflection in Collective Worship, the use of classroom reflection areas and moments of stillness such as observing wildlife or pausing during outdoor learning. These shared practices help pupils express their thoughts, feelings and beliefs with confidence, supporting their spiritual growth across school life.

Key Spirituality Findings from the SIAMS Report (2024)
“The whole school community shares an understanding of spirituality.” We are pleased that this reflects the consistent and shared approach to spirituality across All Saints Church School.
“Spiritual development is successfully encouraged across the school. Opportunities for individuals to reflect and consider their own feelings and beliefs abound.” We are proud this represents the rich range of reflective and meaningful opportunities pupils experience throughout daily school life.
Extra Curricular Provision for All Children
The SIAMS report recognises that All Saints Church School provides a rich range of extra curricular opportunities that enable every pupil to participate and flourish. Inspectors note that pupils experience “opportunities and experiences which enrich their lives at school,” and that the school ensures “obstacles to participation, whether financial, physical or emotional, are overcome.”
Our extensive grounds and outdoor spaces further enhance these opportunities, offering activities such as Forest School, sport, painting, reading and autumn walks, all of which help pupils to appreciate God’s creation and support their personal development.
The report also highlights the breadth of extra curricular activities available to pupils, including choir, cross country running and drawing, alongside wrap around care that supports families at the beginning and end of the day. These opportunities strengthen wellbeing, belonging and enjoyment across the school community.

English Reading
At All Saints, we value reading as a fundamental life skill and place it at the heart of our curriculum because we want our children to be passionate about books, develop a love of reading and access the wealth of knowledge that texts provide. We believe that all children should become fluent, confident readers who can comprehend what they read and express themselves clearly when reading aloud. Through exposure to a wide range of literature and authors, pupils are encouraged to discuss, reflect and share their ideas, helping them to broaden their vocabulary, make connections and draw thoughtful conclusions. We are committed to fostering a culture where reading is enjoyed, celebrated and shared, supporting children’s confidence, well-being and future life chances, while working closely with families and the wider community to promote a lifelong love of reading.
How Reading is Taught at All Saints
Sequenced Reading Lessons Reading is taught through carefully planned, well-sequenced lessons that ensure clear progression in both fluency and comprehension. In EYFS and Key Stage 1, reading is primarily taught through guided group reading, allowing for targeted support, close teacher interaction and opportunities to address misconceptions promptly. In Key Stage 2, this develops into whole-class reading, where pupils engage with increasingly complex texts together, benefiting from high-quality modelling, structured discussion and shared interpretation of meaning. This approach ensures consistency, challenge and depth across the school.
Early Reading and Phonics Early reading is taught through the Read Write Inc. programme, which provides a systematic approach to phonics, decoding and early comprehension. Pupils develop secure foundations in blending, segmenting and recognising sounds, enabling them to read accurately and with increasing confidence and independence. This strong foundation supports a smooth transition from learning to read to reading to learn, ensuring all pupils are equipped with the essential skills needed for future success.
Fluency and Prosody A key focus of our teaching is developing reading fluency and prosody. Pupils are supported to read accurately, at an appropriate pace and with expression, ensuring that intonation and emphasis reflect meaning. Through repeated reading, modelling and performance opportunities, pupils gain confidence and develop a deeper understanding of how voice enhances comprehension. This ensures that reading is purposeful, engaging and rooted in meaning.
Reading for Meaning and Comprehension Understanding is at the heart of all reading. High-quality texts underpin comprehension teaching, enabling pupils to engage deeply with rich language, themes and ideas. Pupils are taught to question, infer, predict and make connections, developing higher-order thinking skills. Structured discussion and opportunities for reflection allow pupils to articulate their understanding clearly and respond thoughtfully to what they read.
Vocabulary Development Vocabulary is taught explicitly within reading lessons. Pupils are introduced to Tier 2 and Tier 3 vocabulary and are given opportunities to explore, discuss and apply new language in context. This supports not only comprehension but also enhances pupils’ spoken and written communication. A strong focus on language ensures that pupils develop the confidence to use ambitious vocabulary accurately and effectively.
Reading Spine and High-Quality Texts A carefully selected reading spine ensures that all pupils experience a diverse range of high-quality texts, including a variety of authors, genres and perspectives. This ensures breadth, cultural richness and progression in reading experiences across the school. Exposure to challenging and engaging literature supports pupils in developing both a love of reading and a deeper understanding of the world around them.
Reading for Pleasure We promote a strong culture of reading for pleasure across the school. Pupils are encouraged to explore books independently, share recommendations and develop their own reading preferences. Opportunities such as story time, book discussions and reading-focused events further embed a love of reading, ensuring that it is seen as both enjoyable and valuable.
Celebration of Reading Reading is actively celebrated across the school through a range of events and experiences that promote enthusiasm and engagement. We mark key occasions such as World Book Day, providing opportunities for pupils to immerse themselves in books through themed activities, shared reading and creative responses. Visiting authors further enrich our reading culture, inspiring pupils through real-life experiences of writing and storytelling. These events help to raise the profile of reading and encourage pupils to see themselves as enthusiastic and lifelong readers.
Library, Wild Library and Year 6 Librarians Our school library and outdoor ‘wild library’ provide welcoming, engaging environments that encourage pupils to read widely and develop independence in selecting texts. These spaces are carefully designed to promote curiosity, enjoyment and a sense of ownership over reading. Year 6 librarians play a key role in supporting these areas, helping to organise resources, recommend books and read with younger pupils. They act as positive role models, fostering a whole-school culture where reading is valued, shared and celebrated.
Reading at Home and Home–School Links We recognise the vital role of reading at home in developing fluent, confident readers. We actively promote strong partnerships with parents and carers, providing guidance and support to enable regular, meaningful reading outside of school. This consistent collaboration helps to reinforce skills taught in school while nurturing a shared enjoyment of reading.
Wider Community Links We value the contribution of the wider community in supporting reading development. By engaging with community readers and celebrating reading through shared events and activities, we extend our reading culture beyond the classroom. These opportunities help pupils to see reading as a lifelong skill, valued both within school and in the wider world.

English Speaking and Listening
At All Saints, we recognise that speaking and listening are fundamental skills that underpin all areas of learning and are essential for future success. We believe that confident communication enables children to express their ideas clearly, articulate their thoughts and engage meaningfully with others. Through high-quality opportunities to speak and listen, pupils develop their vocabulary, deepen their understanding and learn to reason, justify and explain their thinking.
We value speaking and listening as a key driver of both academic progress and personal development. It supports reading and writing by strengthening language acquisition and comprehension, while also building confidence, resilience and self-esteem. By encouraging discussion, debate and collaboration, we provide pupils with the skills to become respectful and effective communicators who can listen carefully, respond thoughtfully and engage positively with others.
How We Teach Speaking and Listening Speaking and listening are woven throughout our curriculum and form a core part of everyday teaching and learning. We provide planned and purposeful opportunities for pupils to talk, discuss and present across all subjects, ensuring progression in oracy skills from EYFS through to Key Stage 2.
In EYFS, approaches such as Drawing Club support children in orally rehearsing ideas, developing storytelling skills and building confidence in expressing themselves. In Key Stage 1 and beyond, pupils engage in structured discussions, partner talk and group work, enabling them to share ideas and learn from others. Throughout the day, pupils are given regular opportunities to share their thinking with talk partners, allowing them to rehearse ideas, build confidence and refine their responses before sharing more widely.
Across the school, we place a strong emphasis on developing vocabulary, with explicit teaching and opportunities for pupils to use new language in different contexts. Sentence stems are used to support pupils in structuring their spoken responses, enabling them to speak clearly and with purpose. Teachers model high-quality spoken language and use questioning, including asking “why,” to deepen thinking, encouraging pupils to expand, justify and refine their ideas.
We place high importance on children speaking politely and with confidence, teaching them to communicate respectfully in different situations and for different audiences. Pupils are encouraged to ask thoughtful questions, listen carefully to others and respond appropriately. Opportunities are provided for children to interact with adults and visitors across the wider school community, helping them to develop confidence in speaking beyond the classroom and to understand the importance of clear, respectful communication in real-life contexts.
Pupils are regularly given opportunities to articulate their thinking through questioning, debate and explanation, particularly within reading lessons where discussion enhances comprehension and supports deeper understanding. Opportunities for performance, such as presentations, drama and reading aloud, help pupils develop fluency, expression and confidence when speaking to an audience.
We foster a classroom culture where all contributions are valued, and pupils are taught how to listen actively, respond respectfully and build on the ideas of others. Through consistent practice and high expectations, we ensure that all children develop the skills to communicate effectively, preparing them for both their education and life beyond school.

Modern Foreign Languages
Learning a modern foreign language ensures every child at All Saints has a real opportunity to learn a foreign language. Learning a modern foreign language offers valuable life and social skills which enhances language skills including listening, speaking, reading and writing.
At All Saints, we teach French as it is a widely spoken language throughout the world, also giving pupils a deeper understanding of the etymology of English words which have derived from French. By learning a foreign language, children gain the foundation to grow into skilled linguists in the future, allowing them greater opportunities in the world of work. Moreover, children gain more than learning a new vocabulary; the skill of learning and speaking a different language builds confidence and resilience.
We use the Language Angels scheme of work and resources to ensure we offer a relevant, broad, vibrant and ambitious foreign languages' curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils using a wide variety of topics and themes.
At All Saints, we enrich our French studies with school-wide celebration days and classroom activities such as Fancy French Days, French shopping and French catwalks. considering how French can be thought about in the curriculum such as science and Design and Technology where children can build the Eiffel Tower. We celebrate the wider community with Europe Day and classes choosing a country participating in the Eurovision Song Contest to discover more about the countries, their culture, language and traditions.
How do we teach French at All Saints?
Our approach to teaching modern foreign languages reflects our vision and is underpinned by high-quality practice. We use Language Angels to ensure learning is carefully sequenced, builds on prior knowledge and supports long-term understanding. The scheme provides an engaging, fun and interactive platform with colourful visuals, catchy songs and games that make language learning exciting.
Language Angels is an inclusive learning platform, supporting mixed-ability, including pupils with SEND, ensuring all students can benefit from learning a language. The lessons are designed to build real-world knowledge step by step, ensuring children learn the language in a clear and coherent manner.
Our curriculum road map shows the progression of French topics as children move though the school.
To enhance our language learning curriculum, we provide extracurricular experiences and opportunities for our children. Currently, we run a Chinese culture after-school club.

Maths
At All Saints Church School, we know that everyone can be a mathematician. Students will develop as mathematicians through carefully planned and sequenced learning that engages, inspires and develops our pupils’ abilities to articulate their thinking. Our pupils follow a scheme of learning informed by BWMAT small steps progression, which promotes a strong understanding of mathematical concepts. Pupils will be able to draw on strategies taught to help them understand, apply and reason mathematically.
The BWMAT Small Steps Maths curriculum is designed to help children develop a deep and secure understanding of mathematics by building knowledge gradually over time. Learning is carefully sequenced into small, manageable steps, allowing pupils to master key concepts before moving on to new learning. This approach ensures that foundational skills, such as number sense, calculation and mathematical reasoning, are regularly revisited and strengthened, enabling children to make meaningful connections between different areas of mathematics. By securing these essential building blocks at each stage, pupils develop confidence, fluency and resilience, creating a strong foundation for future mathematical success and helping every child to achieve their full potential.
We implement a mastery curriculum that inspires children to be the best that they can be, using the Concrete, Pictorial and Abstract (CPA) approach to give children the best possible chance of embedding those core concepts before building on them and applying them.
The Teaching for Mastery Model focuses around 5 strands of Maths and is a sequential model of teaching, which is taught across the school.
The term ‘Teaching for Mastery’ captures what it means for anyone to learn mathematics successfully. Teaching for Mastery consists of the following five components, or strands:
The model consists of:
Coherence - Lessons are broken down into small, connected steps that gradually unfold the concept, providing access for all children and leading to a generalisation of the concept and the ability to apply the concept to a range of contexts.
Representation and Structure - Representations used in lessons expose the mathematical structure being taught, the aim being that students can do the maths without recourse to the representation.
Mathematical Thinking - If taught ideas are to be understood deeply, they must not merely be passively received but must be worked on by the student: thought about, reasoned with and discussed with others.
Fluency - Quick and efficient recall of facts and procedures and the flexibility to move between different contexts and representations of mathematics.
Variation - Variation is twofold. It is firstly about how the teacher represents the concept being taught, often in more than one way, to draw attention to critical aspects, and to develop deep and holistic understanding. It is also about the sequencing of the episodes, activities and exercises used within a lesson and follow up practice, paying attention to what is kept the same and what changes, to connect the mathematics and draw attention to mathematical relationships and structure.
This model is used to ensure that children are given opportunities to develop their own skills and are exposed to each area on a constant basis.
EYFS: In the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), mathematics is taught through practical, hands-on experiences that encourage children to explore numbers, patterns, shapes and measures in meaningful ways. Through play, discussion and everyday activities, children develop their counting skills, understanding of number relationships and confidence in solving simple problems. By being immersed in a number-rich environment, including mathematical vocabulary, EYFS children develop the knowledge and confidence they need for future success in mathematics.
Chilren are introduced to numbers and their values through the Mastering Number scheme. This teaches the children to subitise (to perceive a number of items at a glance, without counting) and to count accurately. We identify and sequence small steps in the reception year, in order to ensure that all children learn and apply the facts and methods to wider problem-solving. Children leave our Acorns classroom with a strong sense of number, feeling confident and able.
Mastering Number continues to be taught throughout Year 1 and into Year 2. It is a nationally recognised programme that helps children develop a strong understanding of number from the earliest stages of their education. Through short, daily sessions, pupils explore key mathematical concepts such as counting, number bonds, place value and calculation strategies in a practical and engaging way. The programme focuses on developing fluency and flexibility with numbers, enabling children to recognise patterns, make connections and apply their knowledge confidently. By securing these fundamental skills and concepts early, Mastering Number provides the strong foundations needed for future success in mathematics, ensuring that children are well-prepared to tackle more complex ideas as they progress through the curriculum.
Learning times tables is essential because it helps children develop confidence and fluency with numbers. Quick recall of multiplication and division facts supports learning across many areas of maths, enabling children to solve problems more efficiently and build a strong foundation for future mathematical success.
At All Saints, we begin our understanding of multiplication using concrete and pictorial methods, ensuring that the children fully understand the calculations before they go on to learn them by heart.
These concrete and pictorial representations are referred to frequently and used to scaffold children’s understanding as they work through learning all 12 of the times tables, ready for their Multiplication Times Tables Check at the end of year 4.
